For Python, we use tools like atheris for coverage-guided fuzzing.\n\n## Key Concepts\n\n### Coverage-Guided Fuzzing\n- Monitors code coverage during fuzzing\n- Uses coverage feedback to guide generation of new test cases\n- More efficient than random fuzzing\n- Focuses on exploring uncovered code paths\n\n### Fuzzing Targets\n- Entry points where fuzzer can inject input\n- Typically functions that parse untrusted data\n- Should be deterministic (same input = same output)\n- Should not have side effects (file I/O, network)\n\n## Atheris - Python Fuzzing Engine\n\n### Installation\n```bash\npip install atheris\n```\n\n### Basic Fuzz Driver Structure\n```python\nimport atheris\nimport sys\n\n# Import the library under test\nfrom mylib import function_to_test\n\n@atheris.instrument_func\ndef test_function(data):\n    \"\"\"Fuzz target - entry point for fuzzer\"\"\"\n    try:\n        # Feed input to function\n        result = function_to_test(data)\n    except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError):\n        # Expected exceptions - fuzzer ignores these\n        return\n    except Exception as e:\n        # Unexpected exceptions - fuzzer reports these\n        raise\n\n# Main fuzzing loop\natheris.Setup(sys.argv, test_function)\natheris.Fuzz()\n```\n\n## Best Practices\n\n### 1. Choose Good Fuzz Targets\n- Select functions that process external/untrusted input\n- Parsing functions (JSON, CSV, binary formats)\n- Data transformation functions\n- Validation functions\n\n### 2. Handle Expected Exceptions\n```python\ntry:\n    result = parse_input(data)\nexcept (ValueError, JSONDecodeError, TypeError):\n    # These are expected for malformed input\n    return\n```\n\n### 3. Seed Corpus\n- Provide valid examples in a corpus directory\n- Helps fuzzer find interesting paths faster\n- Create `corpus/` directory with sample inputs\n\n### 4. Timeout Handling\n```bash\n# Run fuzzer with timeout\ntimeout 10 python fuzz.py -timeout=1 corpus/\n```\n\n## Running the Fuzzer\n\n### Basic Execution\n```bash\npython fuzz.py\n```\n\n### With Corpus and Timeout\n```bash\nmkdir -p corpus\npython fuzz.py -max_len=1024 -timeout=2 corpus/\n```\n\n### Monitoring\n- Watch for crashes and memory issues\n- Coverage increases over time\n- Each run is reproducible with seed values\n\n## Identifying Fuzz Targets\n\n### Characteristics of Good Targets\n1. **Parsing functions**: JSON, XML, CSV parsers\n2. **String/Bytes processing**: Encoding/decoding\n3. **Data validation**: Input checking\n4. **Mathematical functions**: Edge cases with extreme values\n5. **Format processing**: Protocol handlers\n\n### Red Flags (Avoid)\n- I/O operations (file/network)\n- Non-deterministic behavior\n- Sleep/delays\n- Heavy dependencies on randomness\n\n## Reference\n- [Atheris Documentation](https://github.com/google/atheris)\n- [LibFuzzer Guide](https://llvm.org/docs/LibFuzzer/)\n"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":129,"cache_creation_input_tokens":461,"cache_read_input_tokens":18901,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":461,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":1},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"0bab77ac-d1e6-49d6-942a-e5eb0bc8c528","uuid":"c14c9760-9ead-4ff2-978e-c9d0d241996a"}

For Python, we use tools like atheris for coverage-guided fuzzing.\n\n## Key Concepts\n\n### Coverage-Guided Fuzzing\n- Monitors code coverage during fuzzing\n- Uses coverage feedback to guide generation of new test cases\n- More efficient than random fuzzing\n- Focuses on exploring uncovered code paths\n\n### Fuzzing Targets\n- Entry points where fuzzer can inject input\n- Typically functions that parse untrusted data\n- Should be deterministic (same input = same output)\n- Should not have side effects (file I/O, network)\n\n## Atheris - Python Fuzzing Engine\n\n### Installation\n```bash\npip install atheris\n```\n\n### Basic Fuzz Driver Structure\n```python\nimport atheris\nimport sys\n\n# Import the library under test\nfrom mylib import function_to_test\n\n@atheris.instrument_func\ndef test_function(data):\n    \"\"\"Fuzz target - entry point for fuzzer\"\"\"\n    try:\n        # Feed input to function\n        result = function_to_test(data)\n    except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError):\n        # Expected exceptions - fuzzer ignores these\n        return\n    except Exception as e:\n        # Unexpected exceptions - fuzzer reports these\n        raise\n\n# Main fuzzing loop\natheris.Setup(sys.argv, test_function)\natheris.Fuzz()\n```\n\n## Best Practices\n\n### 1. Handle Expected Exceptions\n```python\ntry:\n    result = parse_input(data)\nexcept (ValueError, JSONDecodeError, TypeError):\n    # These are expected for malformed input\n    return\n```\n\n### 3. Seed Corpus\n- Provide valid examples in a corpus directory\n- Helps fuzzer find interesting paths faster\n- Create `corpus/` directory with sample inputs\n\n### 4. Timeout Handling\n```bash\n# Run fuzzer with timeout\ntimeout 10 python fuzz.py -timeout=1 corpus/\n```\n\n## Running the Fuzzer\n\n### Basic Execution\n```bash\npython fuzz.py\n```\n\n### With Corpus and Timeout\n```bash\nmkdir -p corpus\npython fuzz.py -max_len=1024 -timeout=2 corpus/\n```\n\n### Monitoring\n- Watch for crashes and memory issues\n- Coverage increases over time\n- Each run is reproducible with seed values\n\n## Identifying Fuzz Targets\n\n### Characteristics of Good Targets\n1. **Parsing functions**: JSON, XML, CSV parsers\n2. **String/Bytes processing**: Encoding/decoding\n3. **Data validation**: Input checking\n4. **Mathematical functions**: Edge cases with extreme values\n5. **Format processing**: Protocol handlers\n\n### Red Flags (Avoid)\n- I/O operations (file/network)\n- Non-deterministic behavior\n- Sleep/delays\n- Heavy dependencies on randomness\n\n## Reference\n- [Atheris Documentation](https://github.com/google/atheris)\n- [LibFuzzer Guide](https://llvm.org/docs/LibFuzzer/)\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null}}

Extract different types from same fuzzer input\n        string_param = fdp.ConsumeUnicodeString(size=100)\n        int_param = fdp.ConsumeIntInRange(0, 1000)\n        bool_param = fdp.ConsumeBool()\n        bytes_param = fdp.ConsumeBytes(size=50)\n\n        result = complex_function(string_param, int_param, bool_param, bytes_param)\n    except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError):\n        return\n\natheris.Setup(sys.argv, test_complex)\natheris.Fuzz()\n```\n\n## Pattern 3: Multiple Functions\n\nTesting multiple functions in one driver:\n\n```python\nimport atheris\nimport sys\nfrom mylib import func1, func2, func3\n\n@atheris.instrument_func\ndef test_all(data):\n    fdp = atheris.FuzzedDataProvider(data)\n\n    # Route to different functions based on first byte\n    func_choice = fdp.ConsumeIntInRange(0, 2)\n    remaining_data = fdp.ConsumeBytes(size=len(data)-1)\n\n    try:\n        if func_choice == 0:\n            func1(remaining_data)\n        elif func_choice == 1:\n            func2(remaining_data)\n        else:\n            func3(remaining_data)\n    except (ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError):\n        return\n\natheris.Setup(sys.argv, test_all)\natheris.Fuzz()\n```\n\n## Pattern 4: JSON/String Parsing\n\n```python\nimport atheris\nimport sys\nimport json\nfrom mylib import process_json\n\n@atheris.instrument_func\ndef test_json_parser(data):\n    try:\n        # First parse as JSON\n        parsed = json.loads(data.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))\n        # Then feed to function under test\n        result = process_json(parsed)\n    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError, UnicodeDecodeError):\n        return\n    except Exception as e:\n        # Unexpected exceptions should be raised\n        raise\n\natheris.Setup(sys.argv, test_json_parser)\natheris.Fuzz()\n```\n\n## Pattern 5: CSV/Tabular Data\n\n```python\nimport atheris\nimport sys\nimport csv\nimport io\nfrom mylib import process_csv\n\n@atheris.instrument_func\ndef test_csv_parser(data):\n    try:\n        # Treat input as CSV data\n        csv_text = data.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')\n        csv_file = io.StringIO(csv_text)\n        reader = csv.reader(csv_file)\n        rows = list(reader)\n\n        # Feed to function under test\n        result = process_csv(rows)\n    except (csv.Error, ValueError, TypeError):\n        return\n\natheris.Setup(sys.argv, test_csv_parser)\natheris.Fuzz()\n```\n\n## Pattern 6: With Instrumentation\n\nFor better coverage:\n\n```python\nimport atheris\nimport sys\n\n# Instrument the module before importing\natheris.instrument_imports(['mylib'])\n\nfrom mylib import target_function\n\n@atheris.instrument_func\ndef test_target(data):\n    try:\n        target_function(data)\n    except (ValueError, TypeError):\n        return\n\natheris.Setup(sys.argv, test_target)\natheris.Fuzz()\n```\n\n## FuzzedDataProvider Methods\n\n```python\nfdp = atheris.FuzzedDataProvider(data)\n\n# String/Bytes\nfdp.ConsumeBytes(size)           # Get N bytes\nfdp.ConsumeUnicodeString(size)   # Get unicode string\nfdp.ConsumeString(size)          # Get ASCII string\nfdp.ConsumeIntInRange(min, max)  # Get int in range\nfdp.ConsumeInt(bytes=4)          # Get int from N bytes\nfdp.ConsumeBool()                # Get boolean\nfdp.ConsumeFloatInRange(min, max) # Get float in range\nfdp.ConsumeRegularString(size)   # Get printable string\nfdp.PickValueInList(list)        # Pick from list\nfdp.PickElement(list)            # Alias for above\n```\n\n## Corpus Structure\n\n```\n/app/mylib/\n├── fuzz.py              # Fuzz driver\n├── corpus/              # Seed corpus (optional)\n│   ├── sample1.json\n│   ├── sample2.json\n│   └── sample3.json\n└── .venv/              # Virtual environment\n```\n\nCreate corpus with valid/interesting examples to guide fuzzer toward complex paths.\n\n## Error Handling Strategy\n\n```python\n@atheris.instrument_func\ndef test_function(data):\n    try:\n        result = function(data)\n    except (\n        # Expected exceptions - fuzzer ignores\n        ValueError,\n        TypeError,\n        KeyError,\n        IndexError,\n        UnicodeDecodeError,\n        AttributeError,\n    ):\n        return\n    # Unexpected exceptions propagate and are reported\n\natheris.Setup(sys.argv, test_function)\natheris.Fuzz()\n```\n\n## Reference\n- [Atheris GitHub](https://github.com/google/atheris)\n- [Python Fuzzing Guide](https://github.com/google/atheris/tree/master/examples)\n"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":4,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1071,"cache_read_input_tokens":19362,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":1071,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":24},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"0bab77ac-d1e6-49d6-942a-e5eb0bc8c528","uuid":"e439f2fe-2790-4a5f-82c2-180488efe3f2"}

Pick from list\nfdp.PickElement(list)            # Alias for above\n```\n\n## Corpus Structure\n\n```\n/app/mylib/\n├── fuzz.py              # Fuzz driver\n├── corpus/              # Seed corpus (optional)\n│   ├── sample1.json\n│   ├── sample2.json\n│   └── sample3.json\n└── .venv/              # Virtual environment\n```\n\nCreate corpus with valid/interesting examples to guide fuzzer toward complex paths.\n\n## Error Handling Strategy\n\n```python\n@atheris.instrument_func\ndef test_function(data):\n    try:\n        result = function(data)\n    except (\n        # Expected exceptions - fuzzer ignores\n        ValueError,\n        TypeError,\n        KeyError,\n        IndexError,\n        UnicodeDecodeError,\n        AttributeError,\n    ):\n        return\n    # Unexpected exceptions propagate and are reported\n\natheris.Setup(sys.argv, test_function)\natheris.Fuzz()\n```\n\n## Reference\n- [Atheris GitHub](https://github.com/google/atheris)\n- [Python Fuzzing Guide](https://github.com/google/atheris/tree/master/examples)\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null}}

What is the library's primary purpose?\n2. What are the main entry points (functions/classes)?\n3. What data does it accept as input?\n4. What formats does it parse (JSON, CSV, binary)?\n5. Are there external dependencies?\n\n## Step 2: Identify Fuzz Targets\n\n### Good Fuzz Target Characteristics\n- **Input Processing**: Parses external/untrusted data\n- **Deterministic**: Same input always produces same output\n- **Side-effect Free**: No I/O, network, or state changes\n- **Error Handling**: Handles malformed input gracefully\n- **Coverage**: Exercises interesting code paths\n\n### Categories of Targets\n\n#### 1. Mathematical/Computational\n```python\n# Edge cases\ncalculate(value)\ncompute(params)\nfilter(data)\n```\n\n## Step 3: Investigation Approach\n\n### Explore the Module\n```bash\n# Read main module file\ncat /app/mylib/mylib/__init__.py\n\n# Read key source files\ncat /app/mylib/mylib/parser.py\ncat /app/mylib/mylib/utils.py\n\n# Search for parsing-related functions\ngrep -r \"def parse\" /app/mylib/\ngrep -r \"def decode\" /app/mylib/\ngrep -r \"def loads\" /app/mylib/\n```\n\n### Check Documentation\n```bash\n# Look for examples\ncat /app/mylib/docs/examples.md\ncat /app/mylib/README.md\n\n# Check docstrings in code\ngrep -A 5 \"def function_name\" /app/mylib/mylib/core.py\n```\n\n### Examine Tests\n```bash\n# Test files often show how to use functions\ncat /app/mylib/tests/test_parsing.py\nls /app/mylib/tests/\n\n# Look for test fixtures and examples\ngrep -r \"test_\" /app/mylib/tests/ | head -20\n```\n\n## Step 4: Function Selection Criteria\n\n### Scoring Targets\n\n#### High Priority\n- Accepts bytes/strings as raw input ✓✓✓\n- Public API (no underscore prefix) ✓✓✓\n- Used in tests or examples ✓✓\n- Parses complex formats ✓✓\n- Has error handling ✓\n\n#### Medium Priority\n- Requires setup/configuration ✓✓\n- Processes structured data ✓✓\n- Less commonly used ✓\n\n#### Low Priority\n- Heavy I/O operations ✗\n- Non-deterministic behavior ✗\n- Requires network access ✗\n- Complex state management ✗\n\n## Step 5: Exception Handling\n\n### Identify Expected Exceptions\n```python\n# Review function docstrings\nhelp(function)\n\n# Check source code for exception raises\ngrep -A 10 \"def parse\" /app/mylib/mylib/core.py | grep -E \"(raise|except)\"\n\n# Common expected exceptions:\n# -
